questions.question: Explain the different types of electronic transitions involving σ, π and n / molecular orbitals. Give suitable examples for each transition.

  • compounds containing groups such as carbonyl, for example acetone (CH₃COCH₃).

questions.question: Explain the Laporte selection rule and discuss its significance in / electronic spectra of molecules.
questions.solution_html:
• The Laporte selection rule states that in centrosymmetric molecules, electronic transitions are allowed only
  • between states of opposite parity, that is, (g → u & u → g).Transitions between states of the same parity, such as
  • (g →g) or (u →u ), are forbidden. Selection rule -(3 Marks)
  • The rule determines the intensity of electronic absorption bands, with allowed transitions generally being more
  • intense than forbidden transitions. In centrosymmetric transition-metal complexes, (d →d) transitions are Laporte
  • forbidden because both states have gerade symmetry. These transitions may become weakly allowed through
  • molecular vibrations or distortion that removes the centre of symmetry. (or any relevant explanation)
  • Significance -(3 Marks)

questions.solution_html:
• Elaborate on the black body spectrum and the Planck distribution law. Discuss their
  • significance in development of quantum mechanics.
  • A black body is an ideal object that absorbs all incident radiation and emits radiation whose spectrum depends only
  • on its temperature. The black body spectrum is a continuous distribution of radiation intensity over different
  • wavelengths, with the intensity maximum shifting towards shorter wavelengths as temperature increases. Classical
  • theories, such as the Rayleigh–Jeans law, failed to explain the observed spectrum at short wavelengths, leading to
  • the ultraviolet catastrophe. Max Planck proposed that energy is emitted or absorbed in discrete packets called
  • quanta, with energy (E=hν). Planck’s distribution law is expressed as
  • This law successfully explains the observed black body spectrum at all wavelengths and
  • temperatures. Planck’s introduction of energy quantization resolved the black body radiation problem and
  • marked the beginning of quantum mechanics.

questions.question: / Discuss their significance in development of quantum mechanics.
questions.solution_html:
• Elaborate on the black body spectrum and the Planck distribution law. Discuss their
  • significance in development of quantum mechanics.
  • A black body is an ideal object that absorbs all incident radiation and emits radiation whose spectrum depends only
  • on its temperature. The black body spectrum is a continuous distribution of radiation intensity over different
  • wavelengths, with the intensity maximum shifting towards shorter wavelengths as temperature increases. Classical
  • theories, such as the Rayleigh–Jeans law, failed to explain the observed spectrum at short wavelengths, leading to
  • the ultraviolet catastrophe. Max Planck proposed that energy is emitted or absorbed in discrete packets called
  • quanta, with energy (E=hν). Planck’s distribution law is expressed as
  • This law successfully explains the observed black body spectrum at all wavelengths and
  • temperatures. Planck’s introduction of energy quantization resolved the black body radiation problem and
  • marked the beginning of quantum mechanics.

  • radiation and its role in the development of quantum mechanics.)
